build.prompt_version: Trump Diary — Weekly Thread Package Prompt v1

week.headline: The forty-sixth week of Trump’s second term did not hinge on a single shock.
week.summary: The forty-sixth week of Trump’s second term did not hinge on a single shock. It unfolded instead as a dense layering of decisions that, taken together, made the state feel more like an instrument of faction and family than a shared public trust. Law, borders, money, and memory were all touched. Each move was defensible in its own narrow frame. week_summary_notes: This is a cumulative week rather than a single-shock week; the rewrite should emphasize layering and accumulation.
The strongest collision is among weaponized law, immigration-as-control, and crony/private-state fusion.
Information control and memory politics matter mainly because they shape accountability and public trust, not because media conflict alone leads the week.
Security-force logic is present as reinforcement rather than the sole headline.
Resistance and election-engineering are relevant but should remain subordinate to the week’s denser coercion-and-patronage structure.
Administrative capture and executive overreach function mostly as enabling context, not fresh narrative drivers.

rewrite_guidance.opening_focus: Open on the week as a dense accumulation of individually defensible decisions that together made the state feel organized around loyalty, origin, and insider gain rather than neutral public trust.
rewrite_guidance.closing_focus: Close on the cumulative effect: law, borders, money, force, and memory increasingly working together as a single governing style, with only fragmented resistance interrupting it.
continuity_emphasis_notes: Stress continuation over novelty: this week consolidates late-year patterns rather than inventing entirely new ones.
Use immigration and law as concrete mechanisms, and private-state fusion as the moral-political interpretation of those mechanisms.
Where memory or records appear, connect them to accountability and impunity rather than abstract media criticism.
If resistance is mentioned, portray it as partial and uneven, not triumphant.
Avoid overloading the chapter with too many parallel threads; keep the spine on coercion, sorting, and insider advantage.
